html:
Somalis living outside the Somali lands of the Horn of Africa, a community that grew fast after the state of Somalia collapsed in 1991.

Somalis had gone abroad before, as sailors, traders and workers in the Gulf. The fall of Siad Barre and the civil war that followed changed the scale. Hundreds of thousands fled to camps in Kenya such as Dadaab, and many moved on to Britain, Sweden, Norway, Canada, the United States, the Gulf and South Africa. The United Nations estimated that about 2 million people from Somalia lived abroad in 2015. Large communities grew in Minneapolis, London, Toronto and the Eastleigh district of Nairobi.

Money sent home kept families fed and shops open through decades with no working government or banks. It moved through hawala offices, a system of trust between agents that pays out cash at the other end without moving it across borders. These remittances are often estimated at over a billion dollars a year, a large share of the Somali economy.
sum: Somalis living outside the Somali lands of the Horn of Africa, a community that grew fast after the state of Somalia collapsed in 1991.
